title: Shortness of breath at 34 weeks
presenting_complaint: Sudden shortness of breath and right-sided pleuritic chest pain that began 3 hours ago while walking upstairs, at 34 weeks of pregnancy.
history: G2P1, 34 weeks pregnant. The pregnancy has been uncomplicated; she flew back from a family visit (9-hour flight) five days ago. No haemoptysis, no fever. She denies calf pain or leg swelling. No previous VTE, no known thrombophilia, non-smoker. She takes only prenatal vitamins.

findings.name: General examination
findings.value: Alert, anxious, speaking in short sentences

findings.name: Leg examination
findings.value: No oedema, calves soft and non-tender

findings.name: ECG
findings.value: Sinus tachycardia 118/min, S1Q3T3 pattern, T-wave inversion V1–V3

findings.name: Arterial blood gas on room air
D-dimer
findings.value: 3.8 mg/L (of limited value in the third trimester)

findings.name: Bedside echocardiography
findings.value: Dilated right ventricle, normal LV function

findings.name: CTPA (with abdominal shielding)
findings.value: Filling defects in the right lower lobe segmental arteries

diagnosis_options.label: Pulmonary embolism
diagnosis_options.explanation: Sudden dyspnoea and pleuritic chest pain at 34 weeks after a 9-hour flight, with tachycardia, hypoxaemia, S1Q3T3 pattern, dilated right ventricle and filling defects on CTPA — confirmed pulmonary embolism.

diagnosis_options.label: Peripartum cardiomyopathy
diagnosis_options.explanation: Would usually present with progressive dyspnoea, orthopnoea and signs of heart failure; bedside echo showed normal LV function and the CTPA confirmed emboli.

diagnosis_options.label: Community-acquired pneumonia
diagnosis_options.explanation: No fever, chest auscultation clear, no consolidation on imaging; the CTPA shows arterial filling defects instead.

diagnosis_options.label: Amniotic fluid embolism
diagnosis_options.explanation: Typically occurs during labour or delivery with sudden collapse, hypoxia and coagulopathy; this patient is undelivered and haemodynamically stable with confirmed emboli.

diagnosis_options.label: Spontaneous pneumothorax
diagnosis_options.explanation: Would show absent breath sounds and pleural air; chest auscultation was clear and imaging demonstrated pulmonary artery filling defects.

management_options.label: Therapeutic low-molecular-weight heparin, weight-adjusted
management_options.explanation: Essential — anticoagulation is the mainstay of treatment for pulmonary embolism in pregnancy and LMWH does not cross the placenta.

management_options.label: Oxygen to keep SpO2 at 94% or above
management_options.explanation: Essential — she is hypoxaemic (SpO2 91%, pO2 62 mmHg) and both mother and fetus need adequate oxygenation.

management_options.label: Urgent obstetric review and fetal monitoring
management_options.explanation: Essential — the fetus at 34 weeks must be monitored and delivery planning coordinated with obstetrics.

management_options.label: Systemic thrombolysis
management_options.explanation: Not indicated in a haemodynamically stable patient; harmful.
